idea.title: The Wave That Climbed Higher Than a Skyscraper
idea.premise: In 1958, a landslide in Alaska's Lituya Bay sent water 1,720 feet up a mountainside.
idea.audience_promise: Follow the chain from earthquake to landslide to the highest tsunami run-up ever recorded.
idea.central_question: How did a wave in a narrow Alaskan bay rise higher than the Empire State Building?

truth.disclosure: This episode recounts the verified 1958 Lituya Bay megatsunami; stock footage is used as clearly representational visual coverage.
truth.reconstruction_note: The exact visual footage is representational stock, not archival footage of the event.

causal_chain.cause: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake triggered a massive rockslide into Lituya Bay.
escalation: The rockslide displaced water inside a narrow inlet.
The bay walls amplified and redirected the surge.
Water reached a maximum run-up of about 1,720 feet.
causal_chain.consequence: Forests were stripped, boats were carried over land, and two people died in the bay.
causal_chain.why_it_mattered: The event showed that landslides can generate extreme local tsunamis even without an open-ocean wave.

promise_payoff.promise: A quiet bay can produce a wave taller than a skyscraper.
promise_payoff.payoff: The final warning reframes tsunamis as a landslide threat, not only an ocean event.

visual_feasibility.note: Twelve unique Mixkit clips passed sampled-frame QA as non-black, stable and semantically consistent representational coverage.

editorial.notes: Story, visual route and factual framing passed editorial red-team; preview review remains before final release.

factual.notes: Core claims are sourced to NOAA and USGS primary or institutional records.

monetization.notes: No graphic imagery or harmful instructions.

sources.title: Tsunami Generation: Landslides
facts: A rock fall into Lituya Bay sent water surging over the opposite shore and clearing trees up to 1,720 feet.
The event is considered the highest tsunami ever recorded.

sources.title: Field observations on effects of Alaska earthquake of 10 July 1958
facts: The Alaska earthquake was magnitude 7.8 and the Lituya Bay wave reached more than 1,700 feet.

sources.title: Giant Waves in Lituya Bay, Alaska
facts: A rockslide caused water to surge to about 1,740 feet and left a sharp forest trimline around the bay.

uncertainties: The exact trigger sequence and measured maximum vary slightly between historical sources; the episode uses the commonly cited 1,720-foot run-up.

editorial_qa.notes: Preview requested by the production owner; final approval will follow visual and audio review.
